articles.title: Yemen: Escalation in the Middle East and Beyond — Mobility Report (20 October - 02 November)
articles.description: Please refer to the attached file. On 17 June 2026, the United States of America and the Islamic Republic of Iran reached an agreement on a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) concerning the cessation of hostilities. The escalation in the Middle East and beyond had triggered a humanitarian crisis affecting multiple regions in an already fragile context. A resurgence of hostilities in recent weeks is placing pressure on humanitarian access and threatens civilian and essential services. Mobility dynamics across the region and beyond due to renewed escalation remains uncertain. The situation continues to be highly fragile, requiring sustained monitoring and operational preparedness. In the Islamic Republic of Iran, the humanitarian situation continues to be shaped by recurring escalations. Disruption to basic services and infrastructure persist while restrictions on maritime and air transports have affected movement and humanitarian access. Overall, population movements remain localized, temporary, and economically driven, with no signs of mass displacement. In Yemen, displacement increased significantly following the escalation of conflict along the West Coast in early September 2026. Between 07 June and 02 November 2026, IOM Yemen DTM recorded approximately 306,391 displaced individuals, the majority of whom were hosted in Ta’iz and Lahj governorates. Many families are experiencing repeated movements and seeking refuge in already overstretched displacement sites and host communities. In addition, as of 17 October, 3,836 Yemeni nationals arrived in Djibouti, reportedly fleeing the deteriorating security situation. In Lebanon, displacement nationwide remains significant despite continuing returns. As of 28 October 2026, 304,520 people remain internally displaced across 528 cadasters, a 8 per cent decrease compared to the previous reporting period (as of 29 September 2026). Returns have continued, with 964,689 returned IDPs reported as of 29 September 2026, marking a 10 per cent increase from the previous round (as of 29 September 2026).4 Meanwhile, cross-border flows into the Syrian Arab Republic are continuing, with a total of 916,973 movements recorded as of 19 October 2026. Sources include DTM Syria, in coordination with border authorities, the Iraq Border Point Commission, and Pakistani authorities. Increases and decreases noted below are week to week changes.
